Kahit pareho ang temperatura, mas malamig ang metal dahil mabilis niyang inaalis ang init sa kamay mo!

Bisan parehas ang temperatura, mas bugnaw ang metal kay paspas niyang mokuha sa init sa imong kamot!

Mas malamig ang pakiramdam ng isang bagay kung mas mabilis nitong inaalis ang init sa iyong balat!

Other rock changes due to intense heat and pressure deep inside the Earth!

Ang meteorite ay tunay na space rock na nakalampas sa pagkasunog at bumagsak sa lupa! Marami ang mabigat dahil may lamang metal, at iniimbestigahan ng mga siyentista para matutunan ang tungkol sa space.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that momentum is conserved before and after the collision of objects
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes momentum being transferred between objects, which is a consequence of conservation, but it does not explicitly state that momentum is conserved before and after the collision. The competency requires identifying conservation, not just transfer.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: just like in a fun game of billiards
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe different types of collisions as elastic or inelastic by providing some examples
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a billiards example, which is typically an elastic collision, but it does not describe different types of collisions as elastic or inelastic, nor does it provide examples of each type. The competency requires describing collision types.

copy.en:
How does momentum move when two objects collide?

It is transferred from one to the other, just like in a fun game of billiards!
copy.tl:
Paano naililipat ang momentum kapag bumangga ang dalawang bagay?

Naililipat ito mula sa isa patungo sa isa pa, gaya sa masayang laro ng bilyar!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagbalhin ang momentum kung magbangga ang duha ka butang?

Mabalhin kini gikan sa usa ngadto sa lain, sama sa malipayong dula sa bilyar!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the indicators for a chemical reaction as color change, the formation of a precipitate, the release of gas, and or odor, or a change in temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a lizard, not chemical reaction indicators such as color change, precipitate, gas release, odor, or temperature change. Unrelated to the competency.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)

copy.en: The monitor lizard, or bayawak, is a big lizard found in the Philippines — strong swimmers and tree-climbers, with some kinds found nowhere else on Earth.
copy.tl: Ang bayawak (monitor lizard) ay malaking butiki na matatagpuan sa Pilipinas — mahusay silang lumangoy at umakyat ng puno, at may mga uring dito lang matatagpuan.
copy.bis: Ang halo (monitor lizard) usa ka dako nga tiki nga makit-an sa Pilipinas — maayo sila molangoy ug mosaka sa kahoy, ug adunay mga matang dinhi ra makit-an.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PAGASA uses data from weather stations, satellites, and radar
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use weather instruments to measure and record some of the characteristics of weather during a school day
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions weather stations and data, but does not involve students using weather instruments to measure and record weather characteristics during a school day. It describes PAGASA's forecasting, not a student measurement activity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: advise our farmers and fishermen
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions PAGASA advising farmers and fishermen about monsoon arrival, but does not involve examining a local weather chart, making simple interpretations, or describing/practicing safety precautions for poor or extreme weather. It is about forecasting, not chart interpretation or safety.

copy.en:
How does PAGASA know when habagat or amihan is coming?

PAGASA uses data from weather stations, satellites, and radar to forecast their arrival and advise our farmers and fishermen!
copy.tl:
Paano nalalaman ng PAGASA kung kailan darating ang habagat o amihan?

Gumagamit ang PAGASA ng data mula sa weather stations, satellites, at radar para hulaan ang pagdating nila at mag-abiso sa mga magsasaka at mangingisda!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkahibalo sa PAGASA kung kanus-a moabot ang habagat o amihan?

Naggamit ang PAGASA og datos gikan sa weather stations, satellites, ug radar aron matagna ang pag-abot nila ug magpahibalo sa mga mag-uuma ug mananagat!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Six Apollo missions landed on the Moon from 1969 to 1972
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how modern research about celestial objects uses new space technologies including telescopes and space probes
assignedReviews.reason: The card lists historical Apollo Moon landings but does not explain how modern research about celestial objects uses new space technologies such as telescopes and space probes. Apollo missions were crewed flights, not space probes, and the card provides no information about research methods or technology use.

copy.en: Six Apollo missions landed on the Moon from 1969 to 1972: Apollo 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, and 17. Apollo 13 had an emergency and didn't land. Apollo 17 was the last and longest!
copy.tl: Anim na Apollo mission ang bumaba sa Moon mula 1969 hanggang 1972: Apollo 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, at 17. Ang Apollo 13 ay may emergency at hindi bumaba. Ang Apollo 17 ang huli at pinakamatagal!
copy.bis: Unom ka Apollo mission ang ni-landing sa Moon gikan 1969 hangtod 1972: Apollo 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, ug 17. Ang Apollo 13 naay emergency ug wala ni-landing. Ang Apollo 17 ang katapusan ug pinaka-haba!

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the appearance of a crescent moon and when it is seen, but does not involve making drawings or a simple model, nor does it explain the motion of the Earth and Moon relative to the Sun. copy.en:
What is a crescent Moon and when do we see it?

A crescent Moon is a thin, curved sliver we see when only a little of the lit side faces us.
copy.tl:
Ano ang gasuklay na Buwan at kailan natin ito nakikita?

Ang gasuklay na Buwan ay isang manipis at nakakurbang sinag na nakikita kapag kakaunti pa lang sa naliliwanagang bahagi ang nakaharap sa atin.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang gasuklay nga Bulan ug kanus-a nato kini makita?

Ang gasuklay nga Bulan usa ka nipis ug kurbada nga kahayag nga makita kung gamay pa lang sa naghayag nga bahin ang nag-atubang kanato.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Moon is about 384,000 kilometers away from Earth.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides a single fact about the Moon's distance from Earth, but the competency requires describing the general structure of the solar system, identifying major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition. The card does not describe the solar system's structure, other celestial objects, or composition, so it only shares vocabulary (Moon, Earth) without directly supporting the competency's action.

copy.en: The Moon is about 384,000 kilometers away from Earth. It's our closest space neighbor!
copy.tl: Ang Buwan ay nasa layong humigit-kumulang 384,000 kilometro mula sa Mundo. Siya ang pinakamalapit natin!
copy.bis: Ang Bulan mga 384,000 ka kilometro ang gilay-on gikan sa Yuta. Siya ang pinakaduol nato sa kawanangan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: there is a side of the Moon called the far side that is never seen from Earth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make drawings or a simple model to show the motion of the Earth and Moon relative to the Sun to explain the phases of the moon that people see from Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about the Moon's far side due to tidal locking, but does not involve making drawings or a model, nor does it explain the phases of the moon as seen from Earth. It is only tangentially related to the Moon's motion.

copy.en: Because of tidal locking, there is a side of the Moon called the far side that is never seen from Earth!
copy.tl: Dahil sa tidal locking, may panig ng Buwan na tinatawag na far side na hindi kailanman natutunghan mula sa Earth!
copy.bis: Tungod sa tidal locking, adunay bahin sa Bulan nga gitawag og far side nga dili gyud makita gikan sa Yuta!
